module.purpose: Provides the default handlers that convert externally pasted or dropped files, URLs, text, SVG, embeds, and serialized drawing content into editor assets and shapes.
module.summary: This module registers the editor's default external-content pipeline and implements handlers for files, URLs, SVG text, embeds, text, native drawing content, and Excalidraw content. It validates and sanitizes file input, derives asset metadata and stable identifiers, uploads or previews assets, creates corresponding shapes, preserves image crops during replacement, positions content relative to the viewport or supplied point, and reports recoverable failures through localized toasts. Shared helpers enforce file limits, center selections, align content to grids, and retrieve asset information from registered asset utilities.
module.businessContext: Supports copy/paste, drag-and-drop, URL embedding, and file import in the collaborative whiteboard product. Failures affect users' ability to bring external media and documents into canvases.

typeShapes.name: TLExternalContentProps
typeShapes.shape:
{
	/**
	 * The maximum dimension (width or height) of an image. Images larger than this will be rescaled
	 * to fit. Defaults to infinity.
	 */
	maxImageDimension?: number
	/**
	 * The maximum size (in bytes) of an asset. Assets larger than this will be rejected. Defaults
	 * to 10mb (10 * 1024 * 1024).
	 */
	maxAssetSize?: number
	/**
	 * The mime types of images that are allowed to be handled. When passed to
	 * the `Tldraw` component, this also reconfigures the default `ImageAssetUtil`
	 * to only accept files matching these types. If you only want to accept a subset of image types and want to additionally block videos, pass
	 * `acceptedVideoMimeTypes={[]}`. A file is accepted if its MIME type is in
	 * this list, in `acceptedVideoMimeTypes`, or if any registered asset util
	 * accepts it.
	 */
	acceptedImageMimeTypes?: readonly string[]
	/**
	 * The mime types of videos that are allowed to be handled. When passed to
	 * the `Tldraw` component, this also reconfigures the default `VideoAssetUtil`
	 * to only accept files matching these types. A file is accepted if its MIME
	 * type is in this list, in `acceptedImageMimeTypes`, or if any registered
	 * asset util accepts it.
	 */
	acceptedVideoMimeTypes?: readonly string[]
}

preconditions: A valid editor instance, rich text content, cleaned plaintext, and default text properties are available.
postconditions: Text dimensions are obtained from the editor's text measurement service.
Multiline text uses start or end alignment according to text direction, while non-multiline text retains middle alignment unless width shrinking changes it.
Content exceeding the calculated minimum width is remeasured with that width as maxWidth and is marked as non-auto-sized.
invariants: The measurement uses the current theme line height, derived font family, and scaled theme font size.
RTL text is aligned to end when constrained and multiline; non-RTL text is aligned to start.
The minimum width is bounded below by 200 and is based on 90% of the viewport width.
edgeCases: Single-line content starts with middle alignment and is only changed to start or end when the measured width exceeds the calculated minimum width.
Multiline RTL content uses end alignment; multiline non-RTL content uses start alignment.
Content whose raw measured width does not exceed the minimum width keeps its raw measured dimensions and remains auto-sized.
Content whose raw measured width exceeds the minimum width is remeasured with maxWidth set to the minimum width.
detail.summary: Computes presentation properties for externally supplied rich text, including measured dimensions, multiline alignment, and RTL-aware alignment. Long content is constrained to a calculated maximum width and marked as non-auto-sized.

specLiterals.role: Default text alignment for non-multiline content.
Alignment for non-RTL multiline or width-constrained text.
Alignment for RTL multiline or width-constrained text.
Viewport-width proportion used to calculate the content width limit.
Maximum width basis for non-multiline content before measurement is constrained.
Lower bound for the calculated minimum content width.

units.name: defaultHandleExternalTldrawContent

detail.name: defaultHandleExternalTldrawContent
preconditions: The editor argument is an initialized Editor instance.
content is a TLStoreSnapshot accepted by the editor's tldraw-content import path.
The handler options provide the toast and message facilities expected by the external-content handler.
postconditions: The supplied tldraw content is processed as external content by the editor.
When point is provided, imported content is positioned relative to that point according to the editor's external-content placement rules.
invariants: The function preserves the tldraw snapshot's semantic content while adapting it for insertion into the current editor context.
edgeCases: When point is omitted, the editor's default placement behavior is used.
A malformed or incompatible snapshot follows the editor/import handler's invalid-content error behavior.
stateMutations: The editor document/store may be mutated by insertion of the imported tldraw content.
detail.summary: Handles externally supplied tldraw snapshot content by importing it into the editor, optionally positioning the imported content around the supplied point.

units.name: defaultHandleExternalExcalidrawContent

detail.name: defaultHandleExternalExcalidrawContent
preconditions: A URL value is available for validation.
postconditions: For an invalid URL, no content is created and the function returns without producing a value.
invariants: Invalid URLs do not proceed to bookmark creation.
edgeCases: When the URL is invalid, a warning containing the JSON-stringified URL is written to the console, an error toast is added, and the function returns.
When the URL is valid, this provided branch imposes no observable behavior.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Rejects the invalid URL by logging a warning, adding an error toast, and returning normally.

stateMutations: The toast collection receives an error toast for an invalid URL.
detail.summary: When the supplied URL is invalid, the handler reports the failure through the console and an error toast, then exits without creating content.

specLiterals.value: Could not create a bookmark from an invalid url: ${JSON.stringify(url)}
specLiterals.role: Warning text emitted when URL validation fails.
Message key used as the title of the invalid-URL error toast.

specTests.when: The handler processes the external content.
specTests.then: console.warn is called with `Could not create a bookmark from an invalid url: ${JSON.stringify(url)}`, an error toast with title msg('assets.url.failed') and severity 'error' is added, and the handler returns without creating content.

detail.name: centerSelectionAroundPoint
preconditions: editor is a valid Editor instance
point provides numeric x and y coordinates in page space
postconditions: If a selection exists, its page bounds are centered on point
The relative positions and geometry of selected shapes are preserved
invariants: The selection's width and height are unchanged
All selected shapes are translated by the same offset
edgeCases: When there is no selection or no selection bounds, the function performs no repositioning
A point at any finite page-space coordinate is accepted and becomes the center of the selection
stateMutations: Updates the positions of the currently selected shapes in the editor
detail.summary: Repositions the current selection so that its bounds are centered on the supplied page-space point. The relative arrangement of the selected shapes is preserved.

specTests.then: The selected shapes are translated together so the selection bounds' center equals the target point, without changing their relative arrangement.
